blocks.text: Four of Wesgro's eight strategy statements bear directly on this study (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p5). The first sets the destination proposition: Cape Town and the Western Cape "top of mind as a leading business and tourism destination with premium products and services". The fourth names new markets and buyers in China, ASEAN, India, Brazil and the Middle East, "while maintaining a continued focus on established markets". The sixth commits Wesgro to "Track and address systemic challenges influencing economic competitiveness", and the seventh to "Provide economic data, insights & analytics for the Western Cape". The strategy's growth-market work, focus area 4, centres on two of them: India and China, whose travellers already reach Cape Town through Gulf and African hubs (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p46, p48). The growth model's acceleration group holds the Gulf, China, India and Brazil (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p20).

blocks.text: The analytical core is a hypothesis tree, in which each entry names a lever on growth and is framed so the evidence could test it. Three pillars carry the tree: Reshape demand, Transform supply and Build enabling capability. Each pillar holds two themes, and the six themes hold twenty focus areas [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026, pp15 to 16: deck not in hand; page citation to confirm]. Nineteen of the twenty were tested against the evidence of a named workstream, and Appendix A1 traces each to the evidence behind it.

blocks.text: The tree disciplined the evidence. The stakeholder work coded each of its 223 insight statements to a pillar and a category of the tree before aggregating them (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5, p20 to p46). Because the study team did the coding, the counts show where views cluster; they do not on their own confirm a focus area. Each later deliverable marked the branch of the tree it addressed.

blocks.text: The workstreams divide the tree between them. The demand and aviation work tested five of the six demand focus areas and the case for routes and seats. The infrastructure work tested cruise, mobility, product, visitor experience and capital. The inclusion work tested community inclusion and, with the stakeholder and infrastructure work, bookability. The stakeholder engagement supplied most of the evidence on climate risk, the flagship nature sites and the governance theme. The twentieth focus area, workforce and service skills, has no workstream yet. The 300,000-jobs ambition has no labour analysis behind it (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p4). Section 1.1 asks Wesgro and DEDAT to commission one in 2027.
